To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UFMylation of ribosome subunit RPL-26 is required for translocation-associated quality-control (TAQC) and for the maintenance of endoplasmic-reticulum (ER)-associated protein homeostasis.

(i) Ribosome stalling during ER protein translocation induces ribosome UFMyation; (ii) Ribosome UFMylation links protein translocation with ER protein homeostasis; and (iii) Ribosome UFmylation promotes the targeting ER proteins to lysosomes for proteolysis.
UFMylation is an evolutionarily-conserved mechanism to remove stalled nascent chains during translocation into the endoplasmatic reticulum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis by which cells ensure the proper folding of proteins destined for the endoplasmatic reticulum (a process called co-translational translocation).

the regulation of protein translocation into and across the ER membrane, a fundamental step of the secretory pathway, which is critical for the biogenesis of membrane-bound and secretory proteins, as well as organelle biogenesis.
the molecular mechanisms by which eukaryotic organisms ensure the quality of their proteins.

ribosome UFMylaiton is a new protein quality control mechanism that enables the degradation of proteins stalled in the translocation channel during co-translactional protein translocation.
UFMylation is a novel quality control mechanism for protein translocation at the ER.

ribosome UFMyation links translocation-associated protein quality control to ER protein homeostasis.

ribosome staling during protein insertion into the endoplasmie reticulum induces the attachment of ubiquitin-like modifier UFM1 to two conserved residues on the large ribosomal subunit protein RPL26, and that RPL26 UFmylation enables the degradation by lysosome of translocation-arrest proteins, but not the degradation of misfolded proteins by proteasome as in ERAD.
UFMylation of RLP26 is required for protein quality control at the ER.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ribosome is a dynamic organelle with multiple quality control mechanisms to ensure protein biogenesis at the ER.
UFMylation of the 60 S ribosomal subunit is a novel mechanism that enables the degradation of translocation-arrest proteins at the ER, which is distinct from previously established cytosol-based RQC.
ribosome staling at the ER induces the attachment of a ubiquitin-like protein, which enables the degradation of the stalled protein, but not the ribosome.
